science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,695 K and log g 4.62 (u1 0.737, u2 0.052): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 5
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 11.5 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 5 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 2.0%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.21%, the light's own noise being 0.06%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. This campaign's three methods give its period (periodogram 11.64 d, wavelet 11.36 d, autocorrelation 11.63 d; periodogram peak 0.76), accepted by the criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43); the star's period is the mean of its 3 accepted campaigns. The map is made at a tilt of 74°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists no other star within 16 arcseconds of it. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 5

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffd2b3, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 18 (May to July 2018): the map's scale, 98% to 102% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 3.5% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · May to July 2018
